import sys
import itertools

def max_painted_sections(n, q, painters):
    max_painted = 0
    
    # Try all combinations of q-2 painters
    for combination in itertools.combinations(range(q), q-2):
        # Track which sections are painted by the selected painters
        painted = set()
        
        for i in range(q):
            if i not in combination:
                l, r = painters[i]
                # Add sections painted by this painter
                painted.update(range(l, r+1))
        
        # Update max painted sections
        max_painted = max(max_painted, len(painted))
    
    return max_painted

# Read input
data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split('\n')
n, q = map(int, data[0].split())
painters = []

for i in range(1, q+1):
    l, r = map(int, data[i].split())
    painters.append((l, r))

# Solve and print result
result = max_painted_sections(n, q, painters)
print(result)

You want to maximize the number of painted sections if you choose $q - 2$ painters optimally. A section is considered painted if at least one painter paints it.


-----Input-----

The first line contains two integers $n$ and $q$ ($3 \le n, q \le 5000$) — the number of sections and the number of painters availible for hire, respectively.

Then $q$ lines follow, each describing one of the painters: $i$-th line contains two integers $l_i$ and $r_i$ ($1 \le l_i \le r_i \le n$).


-----Output-----

Print one integer — maximum number of painted sections if you hire $q - 2$ painters.
